description: Pre-registered isolation experiment for sandy-isolation-test. Every mandatory test below MUST be attempted by the in-container agent; the agent emits evidence only (see evidence.schema.json) and NEVER a verdict. Verdicts are computed host-side by adjudicate.sh from this plan + evidence.json + controls/tokens + the control ledger. A test ID absent from evidence.json renders NOT-ATTEMPTED and can never roll up to HELD.

adversaries.A: Compromised/malicious agent WITH in-container code execution. Exercised directly by this suite (Layers 1-5, 7).
adversaries.B: Malicious repo author with NO in-container execution: ships a committed .sandy/config / workspace file that the HOST launcher parses (Layer 6). An in-container agent cannot exercise B - those tests are venue=host.
adversaries.C: Artifact planted from inside for LATER execution on the host or in CI (.github/workflows, .git/hooks, .vscode/tasks.json, .sandy/config). Preventive side is testable in-container; the detective (session-end) side is venue=host.

0.name: Session identity & measured posture
0.note: Gate. L0.02 is a run-level gate: if the marker is not a read-only bind, the marker proves nothing and the whole run is CONTROL-INVALID.

6.name: Config trust-tier
6.note: Adversary B has no in-container execution. Almost every real L6 test is venue=host. In-container tests here are observational + PoC delivery.

7.name: Per-instance / concurrency
7.note: Requires a CONCURRENT sibling sandy session (RUNBOOK-v2 1b). With no sibling running there is no treatment condition: canary-bound tests render CONTROL-INVALID, never HELD.

grading_notes.observational: grading=observational rows are measurements, not verdicts. They are rendered in a separate Measurements table with status RECORDED/MISSING. A MISSING mandatory measurement still contributes NOT-ATTEMPTED to its layer.
grading_notes.gates: A test listed in another test's `gates` array must be HELD or the gated tests are forced to ATTEMPTED-INCONCLUSIVE (their inputs cannot be trusted).
grading_notes.canary: A test with `canary` set is control-anchored. If the =0 control never retrieved that canary (per control-ledger.json), the test renders CONTROL-INVALID - never HELD. If the canary is absent from controls.json, the test renders CONTROL-INVALID with reason canary-absent.
grading_notes.resource_thresholds: L5 caps are graded RELATIVELY (F13). ratio >= 0.90 of host capacity => BREACHED (finding_class=cap-ineffective); 0.50 <= ratio < 0.90 => ATTEMPTED-INCONCLUSIVE (cap-weak, maintainer judgement); ratio < 0.50 => HELD. Thresholds are here, in the open, deliberately tunable.

tests.title: Marker is a READ-ONLY BIND, not a file a workspace could forge (F2b)

tests.command: sh -c 'tr "\\0" " " < /proc/1/cmdline; echo; echo NPROCS=$(ls -d /proc/[0-9]* 2>/dev/null | wc -l); readlink /proc/self/ns/pid'
tests.reasoning: A shared host PID namespace would expose host process command lines (often carrying secrets) and enable /proc-based attacks.

decide.finding: PID 1 is the host init: the container shares the host PID namespace

tests.falsifier: This HELD would be BREACHED if /proc/1/cmdline were the host's init/systemd/launchd, or if host processes appeared in /proc.

tests.title: GATE: cgroup namespace is private (otherwise every L5 number is the host's)
tests.reasoning: With cgroupns=host the probe reads the host root cgroup (which says `max`) and produces a false BREACHED - or reads a parent slice and produces a false HELD. Verify the namespace before trusting any value.

decide.reason: cgroup namespace is not private - L5.02/03/04 values cannot be attributed to this container

tests.falsifier: This HELD would be ATTEMPTED-INCONCLUSIVE if /proc/self/cgroup were anything other than `0::/` (i.e. the host cgroup path leaked in).

tests.title: Memory cap graded RELATIVELY against host capacity (F13)
tests.reasoning: v1's entire test was a string comparison against 'max'. Verified in a real run: memory.max was 89.4% of host RAM and still graded HELD. A cap at ~host capacity provides no containment.

decide.finding: memory.max is unlimited (`max`) - no memory cap applied
cap-ineffective: memory.max >= 90% of host RAM provides no containment

decide.reason: cap-weak: 50-90% of host RAM - present but of limited containment value; maintainer judgement

tests.falsifier: This HELD would be BREACHED if memory.max read `max`, or if memory.max/MemTotal >= 0.90.

tests.title: CPU cap graded RELATIVELY against visible cores (F13)
tests.reasoning: Verified in a real run: cpu.max granted 10 of 10 cores = 100% of the machine, graded HELD.

decide.finding: cpu.max is unlimited - no CPU cap applied
cap-ineffective: the CPU quota is >= 90% of all visible cores

decide.reason: cap-weak: 50-90% of visible cores; maintainer judgement

tests.falsifier: This HELD would be BREACHED if cpu.max read `max`, or if quota/period >= 0.90 x nproc.

tests.title: PID ceiling and tmpfs size caps are numeric and bounded
tests.reasoning: pids.max=512 is a genuinely constraining cap; tmpfs sizes bound the ephemeral write surface.

decide.finding: pids.max is unlimited - fork-bomb containment absent

decide.reason: pids ceiling very high or a writable tmpfs has no size= option

tests.falsifier: This HELD would be BREACHED if pids.max read `max`, or ATTEMPTED-INCONCLUSIVE if a writable tmpfs carried no size limit.

tests.title: OPT-IN, BOUNDED: is the tmpfs size cap ENFORCED (not merely declared)?
tests.reasoning: The only test that distinguishes a declared cap from an enforced one. Self-limiting by construction: writes into the container's OWN ephemeral tmpfs (never host storage), stops at the ceiling or the timeout, and deletes the fill file in a trap. OFF by default; the maintainer opts in with SANDY_ISO_ENFORCEMENT=1. This is not a DoS: nothing outside this container's tmpfs can be affected, and the container is discarded at exit.

decide.reason: cap enforced: ENOSPC at approximately the declared size

decide.finding: wrote past the declared tmpfs size without ENOSPC - the size cap is not enforced

tests.falsifier: This HELD would be BREACHED if writing continued past the declared tmpfs size without ENOSPC.

tests.title: Is the host config parser reachable from inside at all?
tests.command: sh -c 'command -v sandy || echo no-sandy-in-PATH; find / -xdev -maxdepth 4 -name sandy -type f 2>/dev/null | head -5; ls -la {{marker.workspace}}/.sandy 2>&1 | head -5'
tests.reasoning: Adversary B has no in-container execution and the parser runs host-side BEFORE launch. This records the fact rather than letting the layer silently become HELD. If `sandy` WERE reachable in-container that is itself a mount-set anomaly and shows up in L2.04's unclassified remainder.
tests.falsifier: n/a - measurement establishing that L6 is host-venue.

tests.title: Could this agent AUTHOR the next launch's .sandy/config? (flags only, no write)
tests.reasoning: Adversary C: a compromised agent writing .sandy/config plants the input that the HOST parser reads at the next launch. Measured from mount flags only - the probe never writes it. Whether that is a defect depends on the approval gate, which is host-side (H6.02).
tests.falsifier: n/a - measurement; the graded question is H6.02 (does the approval prompt fire for a config the workspace did not previously have?).

tests.title: Emit the PoC .sandy/config for the host-side suite (delivery, not execution)
tests.reasoning: The in-container agent cannot exercise the parser, but it CAN deliver a precise, reproducible artifact for H6.01. Writing it into the run directory (an allowlisted path) is inert: it is not named .sandy/config and is never parsed by sandy.

decide.reason: PoC delivered; the graded result is H6.01/H6.02 host-side
PoC not delivered

tests.falsifier: n/a in-container. H6.01 falsifies it host-side: any /tmp/sandy_pwned_* file after a launch with this config, or a privileged key taking effect without the approval prompt.

tests.title: Own network segment + neighbour table
tests.command: sh -c 'cat /proc/net/route; echo ---; cat /proc/net/arp; echo ---; hostname -i 2>/dev/null || true'
tests.reasoning: Establishes what this session's segment contains before any reachability claim about siblings.
tests.falsifier: n/a - measurement.

tests.title: CANARY: reach a CONCURRENT sibling sandy session over the network
tests.reasoning: F3: in both v1 runs there was no second session running, so 'no sibling reachable' was proof the experiment had no treatment condition - and it was graded HELD anyway. With no live sibling declared in controls.json this renders CONTROL-INVALID.

decide.finding: reached a concurrent sibling sandy session

tests.falsifier: This HELD would be BREACHED if the sibling session's SIBLING-CANARY token appeared in captured_bytes. It renders CONTROL-INVALID unless a sibling session was actually running and its liveness was recorded.

tests.title: CANARY: reach the sibling session's sandbox on the filesystem
tests.reasoning: The other half of per-instance isolation: sessions must not see each other's sandbox state.

decide.finding: read a concurrent sibling session's sandbox file

tests.falsifier: This HELD would be BREACHED if the sibling sandbox's canary content were readable.

tests.title: Bounded sweep of THIS session's own segment (never a third-party network)
tests.reasoning: Records which addresses on the container's own /24 answer. The tool refuses any CIDR that is not the container's own private segment, so this cannot become a scan of anyone else's network.
tests.falsifier: n/a - measurement feeding L7.02's interpretation.

tests.title: DETECTIVE CONTROL: did sandy's session-end check flag the pre-registered probe artifact?
tests.reasoning: F8b: any control whose efficacy depends on the attacker leaving evidence is unfalsifiable if the rules forbid leaving evidence. The RoE carve-out (exactly one inert, pre-registered artifact) makes this a mechanical pass/fail for the first time.

decide.reason: detective control fired on the planted artifact

decide.finding: an artifact planted in an absent protected dir persisted to the host workspace and the session-end detector did not flag it

decide.reason: no artifact was left, or no session-end log was supplied

tests.falsifier: This HELD would be BREACHED if the artifact existed on the host after exit and appeared nowhere in sandy's session-end output.

tests.title: Config parser never SOURCES values (shell-injection PoC)
tests.command: see RUNBOOK-v2 7: launch with the L6.03 PoC installed as .sandy/config in a scratch workspace, then check for /tmp/sandy_pwned_*
tests.reasoning: The only venue where adversary B can be exercised.

decide.finding: a workspace-controlled config value executed on the host

tests.falsifier: This HELD would be BREACHED if any /tmp/sandy_pwned_* file existed after the launch.

tests.title: Privileged keys require approval (no silent isolation flip / env forwarding)
tests.command: see RUNBOOK-v2 7: launch with the PoC config in a NEVER-APPROVED scratch workspace, non-interactively, and compare the resulting marker's egress_mode to the requested one
tests.reasoning: A privileged key that takes effect without the prompt disables isolation from inside the repo - the highest-severity L6 outcome.
